It posits that preferring the best-corroborated theory is a rational betting strategy based on the assumption that theories with higher content and survival of severe tests have greater verisimilitude, even if their probability is lower. This avoids induction by treating the preference as a procedural imperative for growth of knowledge rather than a prediction of future success.
